verdict.summary: Round 5 finds no correctness, soundness, test-validity, or security defect. The diagnostic remains restricted to the already-failed parse path, preserves the rejected SPARQL byte-for-byte, and cannot affect execution. The scanner distinguishes keyword candidates from strings, IRIs, comments, variables, language tags, numeric literals, and the expanded PN_PREFIX/PN_LOCAL forms; its focused unit tests and public CanaryFailed integration tests exercise the motivating suggestion, non-application, unrelated parse failures, Unicode/escaped local names, and dotted prefixes on the real API path. Keyword-table drift, sortedness, output bounds, deduplication, and arbitrary-input well-formedness are also pinned. The README, public API documentation, error rendering, and design record consistently frame the feature as an optional, non-rewriting, unmeasured diagnostic. This matches round 4's clean finding set, so progress is stagnant under the required scale.
